findings.text: the run's stored negative-control.log records 90 walks and an assertion message this line no longer emits, so the cited artefact was produced by an earlier revision of the fixture; the manifest note and the fragment's figure of 30 are substantiated only by re-running the committed test, which this review did (30 walks, EXIT=1).

the region is held in a module-global list while both sibling regions are context-local, so the station's sweep thread and tick thread (reckon/crew/station.py:67) share one pinned table and one refresh can answer from the other's snapshot and lose its own pin mid-pass; the effect is cost and a slightly older snapshot, never a wrong liveness answer.

the walk is taken eagerly when the region opens, so a refresh of a project whose pointers never reach the environment scan now pays one full /proc listing where the base paid none; a walk taken on the first read inside the region would keep the at-most-one guarantee without adding a walk to the empty case.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit; 92b8064db3 adds the pinned region in reckon/crew/process_signal.py:296-327 and opens it in fleet_state, 7d0b2be51a adds the evidence fragment, and both are inside the declared scope.
item_verdicts.done_when: the section's done-when asks one refresh over 30 live pointers with a fake counting table, every pointer reaching the environment scan, the beat clock stepping past BEAT_SECONDS, at most one walk and each pointer's liveness equal to the per-pointer answers; tests/test_a_station_refresh_walks_the_process_table_once.py:319-338 asserts exactly that count and 245-289 the equality.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is that a station refresh walks the process table once, and reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:1370-1374 opens process_table_walk_once() around the whole _derive_fleet_state() call so every liveness read inside the derivation answers from one /proc walk.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; it declares status complete, both suite arms, the importing-test delta, the ruff result and the negative control, and its commits 92b8064db3 and 7d0b2be51a match the diff I read.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares reckon/crew/process_signal.py, reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py, reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py, tests/test_a_station_refresh_walks_the_process_table_once.py and the evidence fragment; git diff 8b5c440f1d..7d0b2be51a touches exactly those five paths and nothing else.

justifications.durability: reinstating the regression by removing the region makes tests/test_a_station_refresh_walks_the_process_table_once.py:332 redden at 30 walks, which this review reproduced at the base revision.
justifications.evidence: the gate at tests/test_a_station_refresh_walks_the_process_table_once.py:332 measures the done-when's count and both arms ran on all_debug (slurm 1313211 and 1313219), but the cited negative-control.log records 90 walks from an earlier fixture and so does not substantiate the stated 30.
justifications.fit: the lazy _process_signal_module helper and the region contextmanager match reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:1301 and the sibling regions, though reckon/crew/process_signal.py:296 holds the region in a module-global rather than the ContextVar both siblings use.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py:1350-1374 wraps the entire derivation in processes_module.process_table_walk_once(), and the head arm measures 1 walk for 30 pointers against 30 at the base.
justifications.reuse: the search over reckon/ for a generic region owner found reckon/ledger.py:1806 index_reuse and reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:906 review_heads_resolve_once, neither of which owns the process table's cache, and the addition keeps that cache in its own owning module.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in git diff 8b5c440f1d..7d0b2be51a is one of the five declared write paths, with no change to plan state or to any figure directory.
